Loaded by the main pricing skill when the operator asks about per-seat vs per-X, value metric, price unit, or "should I change how I charge?"

content.user_title: Choose a Value Metric That Scales
content.value_statement: Many B2B companies charge by a unit that does not track customer success, creating margin leakage, gaming, or expansion limits. This skill compares pricing units against four criteria and recommends a defensible hold or metric shift.
actual_capabilities: Compares per-seat, usage, outcome, revenue-processed, and hybrid pricing metrics.
Checks whether a metric scales with customer success.
Tests whether a metric is easy to count and verify.
Identifies gaming, attribution, and volume-versus-revenue tensions.
Recommends holding the current metric or shifting to a candidate metric.
Provides migration risks and routes strategic shifts to pricing-tribunal.
limitations: It does not calculate a final price without customer and billing data.
Its case-study ranges are directional, not forecasts.
It cannot verify metric definitions or gaming behavior independently.
Strategic pricing changes require testing and commercial review.

use_cases.title: Audit a Per-Seat Model
use_cases.description: Assess whether seat pricing tracks customer value, usage growth, and expansion potential.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Usage Pricing
use_cases.description: Compare API calls, transactions, records, or outcomes against buyer language and billing predictability.

use_cases.title: Plan a Metric Migration
use_cases.description: Select a migration path, estimate directional impact, and define risks before changing the price unit.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Current Metric
prompt_templates.prompt: Our current price unit is [unit]. Help me describe what customers pay for and where this metric may misalign with value.

prompt_templates.title: Run the Four-Criterion Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [current metric] against success scaling, countability, buyer language, and volume-versus-revenue tension using these facts: [facts].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Shift Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [current metric] with [candidate metrics] using our customer growth, gaming behavior, billing volatility, and top-to-median billing ratio.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Strategic Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend HOLD or SHIFT for [company]. Include the failing criteria, new metric, expected impact range, risks, migration path, and tribunal test design.

output_examples.input: We charge per seat, but our customers gain value from automated transactions. Seats remain stable while transaction volume grows.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: shift toward a hybrid base plus transaction metric. The current unit misses usage growth and creates expansion limits. Test billing clarity and customer adoption before broad rollout.

output_examples.input: Our per-API-call model is easy to count, but buyers cannot predict monthly bills and frequently limit valuable usage.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: evaluate outcome or capped consumption pricing. The current unit creates volume-versus-revenue tension. Confirm outcome attribution and liability boundaries before changing the contract.

output_examples.input: Our per-active-record metric tracks customer scale, has a clear definition, and matches the buyer's reporting language.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: hold the metric. Improve tier prices or packaging instead, because all four criteria currently pass.

best_practices: Provide the top-customer to median billing ratio before evaluating expansion alignment.
Define the counted unit precisely and document known gaming behaviors.
Test strategic metric shifts with a controlled migration and customer feedback.
anti_patterns: Do not change the metric because a competitor uses a different unit.
Do not recommend outcomes without a measurable attribution method.
Do not treat directional case-study ranges as guaranteed revenue results.

faq.question: What does this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It evaluates whether a B2B price unit tracks customer success, remains verifiable, matches buyer language, and avoids usage friction.

faq.question: Which pricing metrics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers seats, API calls, active records, transactions, active users, outcomes, revenue processed, environments, and hybrids.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the current unit, tiers, customer billing ratios, gaming behaviors, and revenue volatility.

faq.question: Can it calculate my new prices?
faq.answer: It recommends a metric direction and migration approach. It does not replace detailed price research or financial modeling.

faq.question: When should I keep the current metric?
faq.answer: Keep it when it scales with success, is easy to verify, matches buyer language, and avoids incentives to reduce usage.

faq.question: Why route a metric shift to pricing-tribunal?
faq.answer: A metric shift changes commercial incentives and requires explicit testing before release.
